745	### D.10 Hash and canonical bytes
746	
747	The layout hash formula is defined as:
748	
749	`geometry_hash = low32( H64( canonical_geometry_bytes ) )` · `visual_hash = low32( H64( canonical_visual_bytes ) )` (the two halves of the former `template_hash`, LY-26 e; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) · `layout_hash = H64( canonical_block_bytes )` · canonical bytes are `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` per field in a fixed documented order, arrays in ascending id order, tombstones retained, derived caches (`version`, grids, leaf cache, PROJECTOR objects) excluded
750	
751	**Variables:**
752	
753	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
754	|---|---|---|---|---|
755	| `H64` | function | 64-bit | the kernel's block hash (xxHash64 / FNV-1a 64 → ADR-LAY-06, kernel D.10 mixing-function ADR note (KRN:480)) | one hash for the whole project |
756	| `canonical_geometry_bytes` | bytes | template-sized | template | rooms by `room_key` with `origin_px` and tile runs, rects in D.9 order, socket and door positions, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines; strings as length-prefixed UTF-8 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
757	| `canonical_visual_bytes` | bytes | small | template | kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
758	| `canonical_block_bytes` | bytes | tens of bytes to tens of KB | the block | counters, bodies, instances, sockets, welds |
759	| `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` | u32 each | `[0, 2^32)` | persisted per instance | drift gate (LY-26 e) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
760	| hash cadence | policy | n/a | this GDD | see Output Range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
761	
762	**Output Range:** `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` are u32, `layout_hash` is u64 and travels as two int32 halves in the payload (hex only in Save/Load's header, SL-2 S-1); none is ever emitted as a JSON number. The kernel's `state_hash` (kernel D.12) consumes `layout_hash` unchanged. **Cadence** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a byte loop over the block in GDScript is not free (the cost is [UNV], spike SP-ENG-1), so `layout_hash` is **never computed per tick**: it is computed (i) when Save/Load captures the block, (ii) once after `restore()`/`post_restore()` and compared with the value **stored by its owner, the Save/Load slot header's per-block hash record (Save/Load owns the stored copy; `layout.state` holds no `layout_hash` field, which is why the AC-130 allow-list has none)** (a mismatch is a diagnostic, not a restore reason, because the kernel owns `state_hash` verification), (iii) in debug builds at the kernel's `state_hash` cadence, and (iv) on demand by the Debug Overlay; the result is memoised on a block `mutation_count` bumped by LM1-LM4, so a repeat call with no mutation costs O(1). **`mutation_count` is a non-persisted, non-hashed derived cache** (it is in no LY-2 table, in no snapshot and in no canonical byte), **reset to 0 by `restore()` with the memo invalidated**, so two equal blocks built by different histories hash equal (AC-172). `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` are computed once per template load and cached. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the stored `layout_hash` had no owner and `mutation_count` was undeclared.)* **GDScript integer rules for the hashes** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: GDScript has signed 64-bit `int` only, and `PackedInt32Array` stores signed 32-bit values. A u32 `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` is therefore **persisted as a signed int32** and **normalised with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` on both sides before every compare** (a stored value read back at or above 2^31 is negative until normalised, and an un-normalised compare would raise a false `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` on about half of all templates); `layout_hash` travels as two int32 halves `(hi, lo)` each normalised the same way. `H64` is the project's own byte-loop and must use **logical** right shifts (`(x >> n) & ((1 << (64 − n)) − 1)`; GDScript's `>>` is arithmetic), and must not use the built-in `hash()`, `Array.hash()` or `Dictionary.hash()` (not stable across builds; scanned by AC-8). A `HashingContext`-based rung is measured in SP-ENG-1 as the fallback if the byte-loop misses its cost line.
763	
764	**Example:** the three counters `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` encode as `3 × (8 + 4) = 36` bytes. A visual-only template edit changes `visual_hash` but not `geometry_hash` or any key set or tile set, so restore accepts it with one diagnostic. A socket `start_px` or wall-rect edit changes `geometry_hash` with every key set and tile set unchanged: on a welded or otherwise non-`FREE` instance restore refuses it (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`); on a never-welded `FREE` instance it is accepted with `geometry_changed_fresh`. A tile-set edit is refused by the key-set comparison, not by a hash — a 2^−32 collision therefore cannot hide a structural change. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

content.content:
### D.12 Detach re-base and components

The detach re-base formula (registry: `detach_rebase`) is defined as:

components of the ACTIVE `welds[]` forest minus the cut seam, enumerated in ascending `section_id` · `C_keep` = the component containing the body's `origin_section_id` (it keeps `body_id`) · `C_new` = the other component (it receives `body_id = next_body_id`, then `next_body_id += 1`) · `m = min(section_id) over C_new` · the new body's `origin_section_id = m` · `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` · `offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) − frame_shift` for `s ∈ C_new` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `origin_section_id = m` was unstated)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `welds[]` ACTIVE rows | list | forest (LY-14: every weld merges two bodies) | the block | the weld relation over sections |
| `origin_section_id` | int | a section id in the body | `bodies[]` | the body's frame anchor |
| `offset_old(s)` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid, may be negative | the block | body-frame offset before the cut |
| `frame_shift` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid | derived | returned so Body keeps the avatar's screen position (PIPE:694) — Body's concern |

**Output Range:** exactly two components (the forest argument); keep-side offsets unchanged; new offsets are differences of 24-grid values, so they stay on the 24 grid; dirty keys `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>` and `SEC/<id>` for **every section whose socket state changed (both sections of the seam, the unmoved kept-side one included) and every moved section**; each of those sections also gets its `version` and `static_version` bumped (LY-12 d). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Example:** home ship section 1 at `(0, 0)` on body 1 (`origin_section_id` 1); derelict B section 3 at `(576, 96)` welded to 1; a wing section 4 at `(1056, 96)` welded to 3. Cutting seam (1, 3): components `{1}` and `{3, 4}`; `{3, 4}` gets a new body from `next_body_id`; `m = 3`, `frame_shift = (576, 96)`; new offsets section 3 `(0, 0)`, section 4 `(480, 0)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Dirty keys: 2 `BODY` (kept body 1 and the new body) + 3 `SEC` (section 1, whose socket state changed although it did not move, and the moved sections 3 and 4) + 1 `S` = **6**, far under `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; the earlier count of 4 missed the kept body and the unmoved section 1, whose open leaf becomes a solid plate. The new body's `origin_section_id` is `m = 3`.

content.content:
**LY-16 — Recording a weld.** `attach_section(socket_a, socket_b, seam_id, welded_at_T)` (LM2, Class A) runs after the Graph's `weld_join` inside Assembly's single `apply` (KRN:197: single commands "whose `apply` calls published mutators on Graph, Layout and Body"). It appends a `welds[]` row `{seam_id, section_a, socket_a, section_b, socket_b, welded_at_T, state ACTIVE}`; sets both sockets `WELDED(seam_id)`; re-bases every section of the absorbed body by D.6 and moves them onto the host body; marks the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switches the variant slots of both sockets (LY-15), **initialises each newly active LEAF closed (`leaf_w = width_px`, consistent with `weld_join`'s new opening starting at `area` 0, Assembly MSA-15) and seeds the last-projected `leaf_w` cache with that value in the same `apply`, so the hatch span is solid from the instant the PLATE switches off; `layout.doors` re-derives `leaf_w` from the opening's `area` in P3 and changes nothing while `area` is still 0** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: BLOCKING, the LEAF slot had no initial state at weld time, so a P2 reader between the weld and the P3 hook saw an open gap)*, rebuilds the grid; bumps `version` (and `static_version`, LY-12 d) of **every section whose socket state changed — the host section of `socket_a`/`socket_b` whether or not it moves — and of every moved section**, and marks the dirty keys of LY-32: `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>`, and `SEC/<id>` for each of those sections. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text bumped moved sections only, so the unmoved host's PLATE → JAMB + LEAF change was invisible to a version-keyed consumer.)* The mated hatch's opening ids are read from the Graph (`seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`, ordinal = the index in `socket_plan.openings[]`) into a derived cache `opening_leaves` (edge id → the leaf slots it drives, LY-11); the cache is not persisted and is rebuilt in `post_restore` (LY-26 d). **Host rule (deterministic, argument-order independent):** the surviving body is the body with the **lower `body_id`** (the older body; the home-ship, built first, in the MVP). `socket_a` and `socket_b` are re-labelled internally by survivor, not by argument order, so D.6's `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a − pos_b` always places the *absorbed* frame in the *survivor's* frame and `frame_shift_px` has one sign convention; content.content: (d) *`version(section_id)`* is a monotone u32, NOT persisted, reset to 1 on `restore` (the Emitter rebuilds in its own `post_restore`; consumers must treat a restore as an unconditional rebuild signal, because a post-restore `version` can numerically equal a pre-restore cached value). It is bumped by `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section`, `discard_section_geometry`, `layout.doors` and Layout's own `post_restore` (LY-26 c, 1 → 2 for a section with an open leaf). MVP has no prop mutator (props are static); the bump list is closed so a Vertical Slice movable prop adds one entry deliberately. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Which sections are bumped (the rule, stated once):** every section whose rect set can change is bumped, *moved or not*. That is (i) every section whose **socket state changes** — both sections of the seam on a weld and on a cut, including the host section that does not move, because on a weld its PLATE becomes JAMB plus LEAF and on a cut its LEAF (possibly open, `area` > 0) becomes a solid PLATE, so a consumer keyed on `version` that missed the unmoved mate would keep passing light through a solid plate (a see-through-but-solid wall, the failure the secondary design test forbids); and (ii) every section whose body-frame offset changes (every moved section). Each such section also gets the dirty key `SEC/<id>`, and both bodies of the seam get `BODY/<id>` (LY-16, LY-17, LY-27). **Three counters, one contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `static_version(s)` is bumped by every cause above except a leaf change; `leaf_version(s)` is bumped only by `layout.doors` (and by `post_restore`'s self-heal for an open leaf); `version(s)` is the EM-20 name and is bumped whenever either is, so a consumer that rebuilds everything keys on `version` unchanged, while a consumer that can patch (the Emitter's static layer, the weld-preview memo) keys the static layer on `static_version` and the dynamic leaves on `leaf_version`. Animating a door therefore bumps `static_version` 0 times; a stepped slide (a Vertical Slice option, OQ-14 c) costs a leaf patch per tick, never a full static rebuild. All three are not persisted and reset to 1 on `restore`.

content.content:
### D.5 Door leaf and passage

The door leaf formula (registry: `door_leaf_gap`) is defined as:

`gap(area) = floor_div(width_px × area, area_max)` · `leaf_w(area) = width_px − gap(area)` · `passes(F) ⇔ gap(area) ≥ F` · `area_pass_min(F) = ceil_div(F × area_max, width_px)` · `leaf_would_overlap(opening, area′, boxes) = ∃ L ∈ leaves(opening), ∃ f ∈ boxes : overlap(leaf_rect(L, area′), f)` (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* `leaves(opening)` is one leaf for an interior door and **both** leaves of a mated hatch, each at its section's body-frame offset, with the opening's single `area_max`)

where `leaf_rect` for a doorway starting at `s` in an E-W wall whose footprint starts at `w` is: hinge `LOW`: `[s, s + leaf_w) × [w, w + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`; hinge `HIGH`: `[s + width_px − leaf_w, s + width_px) × [w, w + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`; a N-S wall swaps the axes. The leaf slides INTO the pocket on the hinge side, so the visible leaf stays anchored to the hinge end of the doorway and the gap opens from the other end. `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect (its `idx` stays reserved, D.9).

**LY-31 — The PROJECTOR contract.** Layout's data module is scene-tree free (kernel H10): a headless test asserts it references no `Node`. A **separate PROJECTOR** (subscriber class `PROJECTOR`, CR-10: "write engine-side *derived* objects owned by its block owner … never writes blocks"; kernel example "Layout → physics projection; derelict content build") builds engine-side derived objects from `layout.state` and the templates; they are never persisted and are rebuilt from the block, also after restore. The object shape (the [UNV] default and the weld spike that measures it) is in the engine feasibility note and ADR-LAY-03, not in this contract. It builds the door, prop and machinery sprites from the rect table and the seam bead, cap plate and scar pieces from `welds[]` and socket state. It fills the Pipeline's PR-5 layer stack (floor z 0 never Y-sorted, floor marks, ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding in tree order wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery, actors; wall caps) and gives every placed SPRITE object (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead or plate piece) the Pipeline's **`entity_id`** (PIPE D.12, PIPE:553: persistent, owned by the state block, stable across save and reload; the third key of `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`, PIPE:1139). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `creation_id` is retired; the Pipeline has no such field.)* **Layout's `entity_id` (publisher-defined, G1; the namespace tag is registered with the Pipeline, Open Questions OQ-LY-ID):** a block-tagged int64, `entity_id = (LAYOUT_ID_NS << 56) | (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | template_local_idx`, with `LAYOUT_ID_NS` a Layout namespace byte in `1 … 127` (GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit, so a byte of 128 or more would make every Layout `entity_id` negative; the Pipeline compares ids as plain ints and only relative order inside one namespace matters, but the range is fixed so the sign is never in question) that Body, Interaction and any other id publisher must not use in its own high bits (so a Layout id can never equal a Body or Interaction id in the same `class_rank`), `section_id` 32 bits at most (`next_section_id` is monotonic and tombstones keep their ids), `kind_ordinal` 8 bits, `template_local_idx` 16 bits. It is a pure function of the block (`section_id`) and the template, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one, and it is never persisted by the PROJECTOR. **Tiles carry no `entity_id`:** `TileMapLayer` cells are not nodes; wall-face and cap tiles are `class_rank` 0 and tie-break among themselves by cell position `(y, x)` (the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`, Y-sort mechanism per SP-YSORT-1 below). Within `class_rank` 2 the doors, props and machinery of one `sort_y` are ordered by `entity_id` alone (they share one rank in the Pipeline; Layout assumes no sub-rank). The *mechanism* that delivers the key (`TileMapLayer` participation, who owns child insertion order) is not defined here and stays gated on SP-YSORT-1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* It writes no block and creates **no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh in MVP**. It never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D` (Lighting's). Its section nodes are parented under Body's per-body root `Node2D` (Body's `body.projector` owns the root and its translation, BDY-33) — the default shape, which the Y-sort spike below may supersede with option B (no reparent; BDY-33 would then own the pose-driven section positions rather than a root). (→ ADR-LAY-03.) The PROJECTOR must satisfy "never hidden" (art bible 6.1) for seam beads. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Prerequisite story — the Y-sort / PROJECTOR scene-shape spike (SP-YSORT-1), done before the PROJECTOR story starts.** The default shape above reparents section nodes under a per-body root on every weld, which sits badly with the Pipeline's single Y-sort scope (PR-5: ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery and actors in tree order) and is [UNV]. The spike tests **option B first**: *no reparent* — every section's nodes keep one parent under the single Y-sort node and each section's position is driven from the body's pose plus `section_offset` every tick (so a weld changes an offset, never a parent) — and falls back to option A (per-body roots, reparent on weld) only if B fails. **Exit criteria:** (1) the PR-5 draw order of AC-123 holds with two bodies in one scene and across a weld (an actor south of a wall over its face, north of it behind it, the cap above both); (2) no sprite changes sort rank across the weld frame; (3) draw calls for the MVP world are recorded for both options; (4) the weld frame costs at most one frame over 16.6 ms on the reference machine once OQ-2 names it; (5) the result is written to ADR-LAY-03. Until the spike closes, AC-140 has no pass line.
====
*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Headless versus windowed.** CI runs `--headless` (dummy renderer). The CPU-only rows (**AC-136**, **AC-137**, **AC-164**, **AC-138**, **AC-139**, the AC-141 estimator) are **headless-capable** and keep **provisional lines on a recorded machine** (the run records the machine's specification, never a named reference machine). The render-dependent rows (**AC-140** draw-call and build frames, **AC-165** weld frame, **AC-123 (d)** pixel probe, the visual rows AC-124 and AC-126) are **windowed / GPU**: they are evidence-only until a windowed runner exists, and never gate. **No reference machine, build type or spec is named or invented in this GDD:** the machine choice is escalated to the user and the technical-director (OQ-2 / X14, which stays open). **AC-164's aggregate (8 actors per tick at most 0.6 ms) is the budget; AC-136's 0.05 ms P99 per actor is the target.** Reference machine: `project.yaml` names none (no performance or minimum-spec key exists at authoring time), so the pass lines below bind only once the reference machine is named (Open Questions OQ-2). Until then each run **records the machine specification and the measured P99 and mean as retained evidence** (`production/qa/evidence/layout-perf-<criterion>-<machine>.md`; a measurement with no machine named is evidence, never a pass), and the pass line is bound when `project.yaml` names the machine. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* If a measured rung misses its line, the fallback ladder of D.22 is climbed one data-layout step at a time; a GDExtension or C# rung needs technical-director sign-off. The cases cover D.22's terms: a single actor, **8 aggregate actors per tick**, and an **Emitter-sized query** (a 288 × 288 px box). Every measurement uses a Godot 4.7.2 release export, not the editor-debug build, a warm-up of 100 calls, and at least 10,000 calls (or 600 ticks × 2 actors).

Which CPU class and which Godot 4.7.2 release export counts as the reference? *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Until it is named, each spike records its measurement and machine as retained evidence (group K); the pass lines bind when `project.yaml` names the machine; a GDExtension or C# rung of D.22's fallback ladder needs technical-director sign-off. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Still OPEN (X14):** the user has not named the minimum-spec machine or build type, and none is invented here *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the machine choice is escalated to the user and the technical-director; meanwhile the CPU-only rows AC-136 and AC-137 keep provisional lines on a recorded machine and the render-dependent rows are evidence-only until a windowed runner exists, group K)*; the D5 pre-ruling (withhold the lowest failing zoom step rather than cut content) is the Pipeline's. | user (target hardware), agent: technical-director / producer | ADR | before the first performance test is written |
